cards.title: Pediatrician: Human Connection Matters More Than AI
cards.body: A pediatrician argues that loss of human connection is the biggest threat to children, not technology. The solution is spending more time talking openly with each other rather than worrying about screens.

cards.title: Music and Parenting: Letting Go of Snobbery
cards.body: A parent discovers that their children's music taste is valid, even if different from their own. The lesson: kids know a good tune when they hear one, regardless of generational preferences.

cards.title: Signs Your Child Is About to Have a Meltdown
cards.body: What appears as a sudden meltdown usually starts with two predictable changes in behavior. Understanding these early warning signs can help parents intervene before emotions escalate.

cards.title: Low-Demand Parenting and Autistic Burnout
cards.body: Having less conflict at home isn't the same as recovery for neurodivergent children. Understanding the difference between burnout and being stuck in a loop requires looking at what research actually supports.

cards.title: Children Deserve More Than Our Anger
cards.body: A personal perspective on what healing means when children still need protection and belonging. After homelessness and family tragedy, the author explores how to break cycles of harm.

cards.title: A New Mom's Perspective on Motherhood
cards.body: Pre- and post-birth experiences offer valuable lessons about motherhood that often get forgotten. Giving voice to these moments helps us understand what we lose in the forgetting.

cards.title: College Sorority Rush: Moms and Daughters
cards.body: Parents are increasingly hiring consultants for their daughters' sorority decisions. Mothers can better support this process by modeling intentionality and self-awareness rather than overstepping.
